entry.title: Fitting shapes and opening lids
entry.summary: Davies’s hand activities follow familiar movements: fitting, releasing, turning, and using two hands together. The useful choice is the movement your child wants to repeat.
entry.cue: They may be returning to the same lid, shape, peg, or ring.
detail: Her examples include rings on a peg, shapes through an opening, and boxes with sliding lids or bins. A child can explore taking pieces off before putting them back. Color or size matching may come later within the same material.

She suggests simplifying a shape sorter to an easier shape, then adding challenge when it is welcome. These are material examples, not a required collection. Small parts require adult supervision; the book does not make every household closure or loose object suitable for a toddler.

displayContext.footer: You don’t need a different home. Start with what you have.
displayContext.colophon: Original summaries inspired by The Montessori Baby and The Montessori Toddler. Open any idea for its book references. The illustration is an invitation to explore, rather than a room to reproduce. Follow your child’s pace.
